message:
OPERATOR DIRECTIVE — HIGH PRIORITY (P0): Fix the Jarvis command-execution design that is blocking integration.

We reproduced the problem on the operator's Linux home client: run_command sleep 8s with timeoutSeconds=3 returned a pollable ToolOperation job but its underlying process was killed (ToolCompleted, ExitCode=-1, TimedOut=true); with timeoutSeconds=20 it completed; the dedicated start_job sleep 9s completed normally via get_job_result. Source: Client/Modules/ClientShell.fs defaults process deadline to 60s through BoundedProcess.run; Client/SignalR/Client.fs promotes the TOOL CALL after ~3s but does not suspend the process deadline; Client/Modules/JobManager.fs already implements managed long-running OS jobs.

1) Add a concrete P0 task to converge run_command/start_job into ONE job-based execution operation: every process is a managed job; if it finishes within a short initial response threshold return its terminal result, otherwise return the process job handle. Response latency is NOT a process lifetime limit. Reuse JobManager; preserve project/worktree permissions, output bounds, cancel/poll, canonical job outcome; make process exit status unambiguous. No hidden default process-kill deadline; explicit optional user-requested deadline can be separately supported. Assign an eligible worker and provide Manager executable dispatch, not just a plan/status document. Only Manager launches agents. Independently review and integrate through Integrator.

2) IMMEDIATE RELEASE GATE ACTION, DO NOT WAIT FOR API REFACTOR: rerun the exact full Linux .NET11 Client Release suite using the existing start_job(executable="dotnet", args=["test","Client.Tests/Client.Tests.fsproj","-c","Release","--nologo"]) and poll get_job_result through real OS-process completion. Do NOT use run_command with 165/180s process timeout, and do NOT treat a tool-job completion as evidence the process ran to completion. Run relevant Server Release as needed; capture exact source SHA, test counts/failures and final process exit code. The prior 165/180s timeouts arose from the execution wrapper, not an established hanging test. Worker10 can own the gate, but avoid duplicate Worker10 activation while Working.

3) Once a real scoped acceptance result is available, unblock and integrate ALREADY INDEPENDENTLY ACCEPTED waiting changes, specifically per-account server-stored AGENTS.md: Worker9 corrected commit 2e4f470177fc76d45d698f11cf6d67566e87f40d accepted review 6af7d25b331f4e1a9df39ee4426e75c1; integration branch commit 47236e98f; submission ed136921a4024773843f416f58958b9e remains Pending. Ensure Integrator processes it to main with relevant merge/integration proof; do not require unrelated Work migration/recovery/cutover gates merely to merge isolated feature. Respect meaningful test failures and independent review, but reassess blanket gates when unrelated or self-imposed.

This is an operator priority correction. Make an ACTUAL runnable task/assignment and tangible merge progress, not another sequence of speculative verification prerequisites. Do not deploy/restart or activate Work migration without operator authorization.
